title: Token Scenario Timeline & Pricing Scenario Builder
creator: Jon Park
description: Design and prototype an interactive Token Scenario Timeline and Pricing Scenario Builder inside Redwood Console. The feature lets product/finance engineers and platform teams simulate pricing changes, test rollout strategies, and export token-level cost attributions across time. It should combine a time-series view of token usage with explorable attribution breakdowns (route/model/prompt slice), a sliders-based pricing scenario editor (per-token price, quantization tiers, caching), and CSV/JSON export. Deliver a high-fidelity Figma prototype, interaction spec for engineering, and a short usability test script.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity Figma prototype covers primary flows: load historical range, create pricing scenario, run simulation, view per-token breakdown, and export results
Timeline UI displays hourly/daily aggregations with drill-to-route and drill-to-model attribution
Scenario editor allows toggling pricing levers: per-token rate, billing unit (prompt/response), caching savings %, and quantization multiplier
Export produces a CSV with timestamp, route, model, token_count, effective_price, and attribution_reason fields
Design spec includes accessibility guidance (color contrast, keyboard nav for timeline scrubbing) and responsive behaviors for >1024px and 768–1024px widths
Engineering sign-off: prototype interactions mapped to frontend components and data contracts with ENG-21234 owner
design_notes: Primary persona: Platform/Finance engineers who need to evaluate cost impact of model/quantization/rollout decisions
Timeline should support multiple scenarios overlayed for comparison; use semi-transparent bands with distinct colorblind-friendly palette
Default aggregation buckets: last 30 days daily, last 72 hours hourly; allow custom range selection
Attribution panel to the right shows stacked breakdown by route, model variant, and prompt slice; primary sort by cost contribution
Scenario editor placed in a slide-over panel to preserve timeline context; include quick presets (Conservative, Balanced, Aggressive)
Export schema must align with analytics events used by billing team to enable reproducible audits
decisions: Use slide-over for scenario editor instead of modal to keep timeline context visible
Adopt CSV first for export, with JSON export as secondary (engineering effort to normalize nested attribution omitted)
Show scenario comparison up to three overlays to avoid visual clutter
Integrate with Rollouts: include a toggle to simulate canary rollout percentages (10/25/50/100) applied to scenarios
open_questions: How granular should credits/discounts be modeled in scenarios (per-customer, per-route, or global)? Need PM decision
What is the canonical source for historical token attribution data and availability window? (ENG to confirm SLA)
Should exported attribution include hashes for privacy (anonymous route identifiers) or full route names for internal audits?
Is there appetite to surface cost estimates per SDK call (client-side sampling) in a subsequent phase?
